title: Chapter 80
content:
The heat haze shimmered off the asphalt like rising steam while the car sat idling at a red light. A severe heatwave advisory blared across the airwaves, leaving the mid-afternoon streets unusually deserted.

The light flicked green, and Jakyeong eased his foot onto the accelerator.

The GPS was tracking toward a luxury high-rise hotel in downtown Seoul. Wang Ryun’s girlfriend had quietly slipped back into the country, and with nowhere safe to lie low on short notice, she was holding out in a private hotel suite.

"Has President Kang been tied up with business lately?" Ryun asked from the passenger seat, turning to study his younger brother.

Jakyeong gave a faint, indifferent shake of his head. "How would I know?"

Ever since that lavish birthday dinner at the main family estate, Kang Il-hyun had practically vanished. He left the grounds at dawn and returned well past midnight. According to the senior housekeeper, taking a few days of impromptu leave meant corporate matters had piled up to his neck.

I assumed all he did was chop off people's limbs for sport, Jakyeong mused. Fascinating to know he actually works for a living.

Slipping into the subterranean hotel garage, the three operatives took the elevator up to the lobby.

While Ryun disappeared upstairs to rendezvous with his girlfriend, Wang Han and Jakyeong settled into a quiet lounge area to wait. Han casually watched the coming and going of wealthy patrons, while Jakyeong pulled up the target dossier Park Tae-soo had transmitted the previous afternoon.

The mark was a man named Kim Dong-myung—a face Jakyeong recognized instantly.

He had crossed paths with the man a year ago while shadowing Kang Seok-joo at an underground auction. Kim was a broker who displayed and traded human beings like livestock—the very degenerate who had casually leaned in to whisper that he could procure prepubescent children if the price was right.

Kim ran dozens of high-end trafficking brothels spanning Seoul, Busan, Tokyo, and Hong Kong. The illicit revenue filtered directly into the private coffers of Director Kim of the Haewon Group—a key faction leader loyal to Chairman Kang, and an open obstacle to Il-hyun's rise.

Kang Il-hyun was methodically trimming the canopy before felling the trunk.

And he was using Jakyeong and his brothers as the axe.

Tiring of the dossier, Jakyeong was casually tapping through a mobile game when Wang Han tapped his forearm, gesturing toward the center of the grand lobby.

Jakyeong looked up, expecting Ryun, but his eyes caught on a familiar frame.

Kang Il-hyun.

Why the notoriously busy CEO was roaming a luxury hotel lobby in broad daylight was anyone's guess, but he wasn't alone. Walking at his side was a young woman in a chic, tailored black dress—someone Jakyeong had never seen before. Her designer clutch and polished demeanor were far too glamorous for a secretary, and the easy rapport between them carried an unmistakable air of intimacy.

Jakyeong had never seen Il-hyun laugh with a woman like that.

When Il-hyun shook his head with an amused, helpless shrug, the woman beamed back with radiant delight. Han and Jakyeong subtly turned their shoulders away, sinking into their chairs to avoid crossing lines of sight.

Moments later, the pair stepped into the private VIP lift and vanished upstairs.

Han sneaked a cautious sideways glance at Jakyeong's stone-cold profile. "Must be here on corporate business. Should we have gone over to pay our respects?"

"Why bother?"

Jakyeong offered a flat, clipped response, keeping his eyes pinned to his phone screen as he aggressively tapped through his game.

Nearly half an hour later, Wang Ryun sauntered out of the elevators. His linen shirt was half-unbuttoned and his neck flushed a deep, telltale crimson—a clear testament to a heated reunion.

Han gave him a look of deep exasperation, telling him to button his collar, but Ryun merely flashed a shameless, roguish grin.

"Place is packed even in the middle of the day. Guess everyone's hiding a lover in these rooms like me, huh?"

Han shot him a warning glare to shut his mouth, but Ryun chuckled, making crude jokes about the unmatched superiority of an afternoon romp. Shaking their heads at the vulgar display, they escorted their rowdy brother out to the garage.

Cruising back toward the district, Ryun spotted a luxury department store across the avenue. "Wei, didn't you mention you wanted to stop by the boutique counters earlier?"

"Forget it. Don't need anything."

The atmospheric pressure inside the vehicle had dropped below freezing. Ryun exchanged a bewildered, silent glance with Wang Han, receiving only a warning shake of the head.

In the rearview mirror, an unmarked black sedan trailed two car lengths behind them. Il-hyun’s surveillance detail was as relentless as ever, but having given up on running, the tail barely registered.
"Did you truly believe a petty theatrical stunt like this would move me, boy?"

The silver-haired patriarch bore the heavy creases of a long, bloody lifetime across his face, yet his dark gaze held the unyielding, terrifying vigor of an apex predator. Draped in an immaculate gray suit with a burgundy silk tie, a vintage briar pipe resting in his hand, he looked as though he had stepped out of a mid-century cinema classic.

"A stunt? You wound me, Elder," Il-hyun replied smoothly. "When two young hearts gravitate toward one another, who am I to stand in the way of destiny?"

Flanking the patriarch sat a young couple.

The woman in the black dress was an alumna from Il-hyun's university days, now serving as a senior corporate strategist within his network. Seated beside her, holding her hand with quiet devotion, was the old man's sole grandson: the real Jang Yi-an.

The elder was Jang Myung—once the reigning dragon of the Hong Kong triad syndicate. Though officially retired from the front lines, a single whisper from the old patriarch could still sway the underworld across three continents.

"So you expect me to believe... their meeting was mere coincidence?"

"Whether orchestrated by fate or circumstance, does the preamble truly matter? Your heir has found his ideal match. Surely that warrants a toast."

Jang Myung scoffed at the sheer, brazen audacity.

After losing his only son in a tragic syndicate ambush decades ago, the old dragon had sheltered this grandson like delicate porcelain, barring him from setting a single toe near the underworld. While the boy's mother was of Korean descent, the old man had never anticipated his grandson would walk through the door with a Korean woman on his arm, demanding blessings for marriage.

And to find out she was one of Kang Il-hyun’s trusted lieutenants.

"Let us cut the pleasantries," Jang Myung said, his voice dropping into gravel. "State your price."

Il-hyun gave a subtle flick of his fingers toward the door.

Tae-soo bowed, escorting the young couple out of the private executive suite. Once the double doors sealed shut, a server poured two glasses of traditional clear spirits—the Hong Kong equivalent of rough, unrefined soju.

Il-hyun filled the elder's cup before topping off his own. Jang Myung’s gaze lingered on the crystal.

State your terms, and I shall grant them. But utter a single word of insolence, and I will have your corpse thrown into the harbor.

Yet Il-hyun merely turned his shoulders, emptied the liquor in one clean, respectful motion, and refilled his glass in measured silence.

Jang Myung downed his cup in kind. Only after Il-hyun refilled the elder's vessel did the younger man break the quiet.

"I am well aware of the deep, historic ties you share with my father, Chairman Kang."

Jang Myung held his silence, studying the predator across the mahogany.

"I am equally aware of your enduring devotion to the Haewon empire."

"Your point?"

"Back my succession," Il-hyun said, his baritone steady and unwavering. "You know as well as I do that my elder brother, Kang Tae-han, lacks the operational spine to steer the conglomerate."

It was a direct bid for the elder's decisive voting bloc. If the succession war went to the shareholder floor, Jang Myung’s international holdings held the balance of power.

"And you believe you possess such spine?"

"I can guarantee I won't drive the empire into the dirt."

When Jang Myung let out an incredulous scoff, Il-hyun smiled, effortlessly topping off the elder's glass.

"I know I carry plenty of rough edges, Elder. But might you look upon me with the indulgence you once held for your late son?"

Watching the young man pour the liquor with disarming charm, Jang Myung found himself momentarily at a loss for words.

He had prepared to break the young upstart's arrogance with ruthless discipline, only to find a creature far more cunning and slippery than Chairman Kang ever was. Worse still, there was an uncanny, eerie resonance between Il-hyun’s relentless, bulldozer drive and the memory of his own deceased son.

And Il-hyun clearly knew it.

Meeting in private revealed that beneath the monstrous rumors, the man was far more calculated than unhinged. A sliver of cautious respect took root in the old dragon's chest.

"Persuade your father first," Jang Myung said, lifting his glass. "Achieve that, and I will consider lending my hand."

Il-hyun raised his cup in return. As expected, Chairman Kang was the final barrier.

The playbook was clear, though the execution required delicate calibration: whether to strip the old tiger of his claws and teeth, or to skin him alive entirely, was a choice resting in his hands.
Leaning his head back against the leather headrest, Il-hyun closed his eyes as the sedan glided down the highway.

Pouring heavy liquor into an empty stomach since noon had left his temples throbbing with a dull ache. He had vastly underestimated the old dragon’s bottomless tolerance for alcohol, regretting that he had chosen a drinking duel as his opening gambit.

All he wanted was to see Lee Ja-kyeong’s face.

Leaving the boy to rest undisturbed for two full days had pushed his patience to the brink. Having displayed such unprecedented restraint, he wondered if the kid might greet him with a touch of warmth today.

The sedan rolled through the wrought-iron gates of the estate.

Stepping out onto the drive, a distinct splashing sound echoed from the rear courtyard.

One look was all it took. Waving Tae-soo to head inside, Il-hyun turned his stride toward the pool deck, an involuntary, radiant smile breaking across his bruised lips. His pace quickened with every step.

Approaching the coping, he looked down to see Jakyeong gliding beneath the illuminated turquoise water like a sleek, dark seal.

Il-hyun waited at the edge. A moment later, Jakyeong breached the surface, exhaling a sharp, wet gasp as he pushed his dark fringe from his eyes.

"Hello, darling."

Il-hyun offered a bright, affectionate greeting, only for Jakyeong to cut him a single, icy glare before diving straight back under, swimming toward the far steps without a word.

Two days of absence, and I get completely iced out.

Frowning, Il-hyun’s eyes landed on the side table by the sun loungers: half a bottle of liquor sat beside an overflowing crystal ashtray. Far too modest for a gathering, but dangerously heavy for a lone smoker.

Just as Il-hyun debated wading in to haul the stray out by his waist, Jakyeong walked up the shallow steps.

Clad in dark swimwear beneath a translucent white linen shirt that clung to his lean frame, every line of his muscular torso was laid bare. Wringing the water from the hem, Jakyeong marched toward the loungers to grab a fresh towel.

Il-hyun stepped directly into his path, studying the boy's face at point-blank range.

How best to describe this look? A sour, deeply offended feline?

Il-hyun arched a dark brow. "You know you're looking at me with a remarkably vicious glare right now?"

"My apologies," Jakyeong deadpanned, his voice flat as a board. "I was born with a vicious set of eyes."

Offering the hollow apology, Jakyeong whipped around, vigorously toweling his hair as he made a beeline for the terrace doors.

Il-hyun stood frozen in sheer disbelief. Returning home half-plastered purely out of eagerness to see the kid's face, only to be treated like dirt on his shoe, rubbed his temper the wrong way.

He lunged forward, catching Jakyeong’s shoulder and spinning him around to lock eyes.

"If something pissed you off, spit it out. Don't play these childish games."

Jakyeong clamped his jaw shut, his dark eyes narrowing into razor-sharp slits.

Sensing the boy's bristling defense, Il-hyun softened his posture, bringing a warm, gentle palm to cup Jakyeong’s cheek.

The one who loves more is the one who yields.

"Don't look at me like that, darling. It's tearing my heart out."

Smiling, Il-hyun leaned in to press a kiss to those stubborn lips.

In the next heartbeat, Jakyeong’s head whipped backward.

Expecting an evasive slip, Il-hyun didn't flinch—only for Jakyeong’s forehead to slam forward with explosive, concussive force.

CRACK.

The brutal headbutt connected flush against the bridge of Il-hyun's nose.

Il-hyun stumbled back, clutching his face with a sharp, agonizing wince.

Standing before him with that same venomous, unrepentant glare, Jakyeong curled his lips into a rotting, sarcastic smirk.

"My apologies. It was an accident."

An accident? You put your entire body weight into that strike, you little monster.

Before Il-hyun could even lower his hands to roar, Jakyeong pivoted on his heel and bolted through the terrace doors, disappearing up the grand staircase.

Throbbing pain radiated across Il-hyun's nasal bone. Fuming, he moved to pursue the boy, but halted in the foyer under the watchful eyes of several domestic staff.

Grinding his molars together, Il-hyun glared up at the empty second-floor landing.

What in the absolute hell did I do this time?
